title: Aegis Verifier
summary: Make an AI agent commit to a trade claim, then check it against a live Pyth price and your policy before any escrowed funds move.
what: Aegis is an Anchor 0.31.1 verification layer for agent trades. Agents stake SOL to register. Owners lock tokens in escrow and set a policy. The agent first commits a hash of its claim, then reveals it in verify_and_execute; the program checks the hash, the Pyth oracle price and the policy, then executes or refunds and slashes.
app_note: The page at /dapps/aegis/ is the generic IDL-driven wallet console. The lab tree is branch sol-college-devnet of Blockchains/aegis-verifier.

try_steps.do: Open /dapps/aegis/, switch to Devnet, and connect a wallet. The lab already ran an approved and a rejected verification.
try_steps.see: Escrow D9L58YBh… is Executed; the second escrow is Refunded.
try_steps.ran: lock_escrow H5oyPmM6…; commit 5RM2QsJt…; verify_and_execute 64X9jV2U…; mismatch T9FbhWU3…

diagram: agent --register_agent(stake)--> reputation; owner --configure_policy--> policy; owner --lock_escrow--> vault; agent --commit(hash)--> escrow Committed; agent --verify_and_execute(claim, Pyth)--> Executed (pay owner dest) | Refunded (refund owner, slash).
innovation: Commit-reveal stops an agent from picking its claim after seeing the price, and the oracle check plus on-chain policy decide execution without trusting the agent.
exercises: Why must the claim hash be committed before verify_and_execute?
What happens to the escrow if the claimed price is more than 1% from Pyth?
